### Q24. An indwelling catheter drainage bag is found above the level of the bladder. What should the nurse do?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Reposition the bag below bladder level and assess drainage
- **B.** Disconnect the catheter to drain the bag
- **C.** Place the bag directly on the floor
- **D.** Keep it elevated to increase urine collection

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Reposition the bag below bladder level and assess drainage**

Bladder urine ka storage organ hai aur drainage bag tak urine gravity se jaata hai. Jab bag bladder se upar hota hai, drainage ruk sakti hai aur contaminated urine ke wapas jaane ka risk badh sakta hai. Bag ko bladder ke neeche, floor se upar, aur tubing ko kink-free rakho.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Sahi):** Bag neeche rakhne se gravity drainage restore ho sakti hai. Nurse urine flow aur patient ke symptoms bhi check karti hai.
- **B (Galat):** Connection kholna unnecessary hai aur germs ko andar aane ka rasta de sakta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Floor se bag contaminate ho sakta hai. Use suitable support par rakhna chahiye.
- **D (Galat):** Bag upar karne se gravity drainage behtar nahi hoti aur reverse flow ka risk ho sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** Bag below bladder, off floor, no kinks.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://www.cdc.gov/infection-control/hcp/cauti/summary-of-recommendations.html).

**YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.
</details>

Source topic Q2.

### Q65. Which is an appropriate indication for an indwelling urinary catheter?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Preventing every episode of nocturia
- **B.** Acute urinary retention when catheterization is clinically indicated
- **C.** Replacing all toilet assistance in independent patients
- **D.** Routine convenience for every ambulatory patient

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Acute urinary retention when catheterization is clinically indicated**

Urinary retention ka matlab hai ki bladder mein urine jama hai, lekin patient usse theek se bahar nahi nikaal pa raha. Jab acute retention clinically confirm ho aur catheter ki zarurat ho, drainage se bladder ka pressure aur discomfort kam hota hai. Nurse indication aur alternatives assess karti hai aur authorized protocol follow karti hai.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Galat):** Raat ko baar-baar urine aana nocturia hai. Is symptom ki wajah assess karni chahiye, routine catheter lagana zaroori nahi hai.
- **B (Sahi):** Acute retention mein indicated catheter bladder ko drain kar sakti hai. Iski zarurat roz review karni chahiye.
- **C (Galat):** Independent patient ko toilet access dena behtar hai. Catheter toileting assistance ka routine substitute nahi hai.
- **D (Galat):** Chal sakne wale patient ki convenience catheter-related infection aur trauma ka extra risk justify nahi karti.

**Exam clue:** Retention aur incontinence alag problems hain. Catheter sirf appropriate indication ke liye lagti hai.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://www.cdc.gov/infection-control/hcp/cauti/summary-of-recommendations.html).

**YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.
</details>

### Q79. A catheterized patient has no urine in the bag for two hours and reports suprapubic discomfort. What should the nurse do first?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Assess the patient and check for kinks, obstruction and bladder distension
- **B.** Increase IV fluids regardless of fluid status
- **C.** Assume the kidneys have permanently failed
- **D.** Forcefully irrigate the catheter without an order

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Assess the patient and check for kinks, obstruction and bladder distension**

Suprapubic discomfort ka matlab lower abdomen mein bladder ke upar dard ya pressure hai. Urine bag khaali ho aur discomfort ho toh pehle patient ki condition, tubing ki position aur bladder distension check karo. Kink hatane par bhi flow na aaye toh timely escalation aur protocol ke hisaab se bladder assessment chahiye.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Sahi):** Patient aur drainage pathway dono check karne se blockage aur low production ke beech farq samajhne mein madad milti hai.
- **B (Galat):** Bina fluid status jaane fluids badhane se retention solve nahi hoti aur overload ho sakta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Do ghante ki absent drainage se permanent renal failure prove nahi hota. Mechanical blockage bhi ho sakta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Forceful irrigation mucosa ko damage kar sakti hai. Irrigation sirf specific indication aur authorized protocol ke mutabik honi chahiye.

**Exam clue:** No drainage plus bladder discomfort suggests possible obstruction. Assess first, escalate promptly.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK596722/).

**YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.
</details>

Source topic Q4.

### Q112. Why should a urinary drainage system normally remain closed?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** The bag must never be emptied under any circumstances
- **B.** A closed system stops all urine flow
- **C.** Opening connections can introduce microorganisms into the urinary tract
- **D.** The system is used to measure arterial pressure

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Opening connections can introduce microorganisms into the urinary tract**

Closed system ka matlab hai ki catheter aur collecting tubing ka connection unnecessary khola nahi jaata. Microorganisms connection se enter karke urinary tract tak pahunch sakte hain. Bag ka approved outlet emptying ke liye use hota hai aur usko clean rakha jaata hai.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Galat):** Bag bharne se pehle usse designated outlet se safely empty karna zaroori hai.
- **B (Galat):** Closed system mein urine freely drain ho sakta hai. Closed ka matlab blocked nahi hota.
- **C (Sahi):** Unnecessary disconnection se contamination ka rasta banta hai. Isliye aseptic closed drainage maintain karte hain.
- **D (Galat):** Arterial pressure blood pressure hai aur uske liye alag monitoring equipment use hota hai.

**Exam clue:** Drainage outlet use karo, catheter-tubing junction ko routine mein mat kholo.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://www.cdc.gov/infection-control/hcp/cauti/summary-of-recommendations.html).

**Related exam evidence:** [RRB Nursing Superintendent, 12 March 2026 Shift 2 — third-party reported concept](https://testbook.com/question-answer/in-a-situation-where-an-indwelling-urinary-cathete--69df45cc13e74fe439d55a62). Reported key option 3, not an authenticated exact match.

**YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.
</details>

## Mock 02

Source: `Chapters/Nursing-Foundations/Mock-Tests/Nursing-Foundations-Mock-02-120.md` (blob `7d36d845e08e3c53e1b84a4f51d93fe70118ee4c`)

### Q13. Which practice helps prevent urethral traction from an indwelling catheter?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Use an appropriate securement device and allow adequate slack
- **B.** Attach the tubing tightly so the catheter pulls during movement
- **C.** Leave the heavy drainage bag hanging from the catheter
- **D.** Tie the tubing to a moving bed rail with no slack

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Use an appropriate securement device and allow adequate slack**

Traction ka matlab catheter se urethra par khinchav padna hai. Jab patient hilta hai ya bag heavy hota hai, tube kheench sakti hai aur dard, bleeding ya tissue damage ho sakta hai. Appropriate securement aur enough slack movement ke dauran is khinchav ko kam karte hain.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Sahi):** Suitable securement catheter ko stable rakhta hai aur slack patient movement allow karta hai. Site anatomy aur policy par depend karti hai.
- **B (Galat):** Tube tight rakhna movement ko catheter par transfer karta hai aur trauma ka risk badhata hai.
- **C (Galat):** Bag ka weight catheter par padne se urethra par pull badhta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Moving rail se tube bandhne par rail upar-neeche hone se catheter khinch sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** Secure catheter and support bag separately.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://www.cdc.gov/infection-control/hcp/cauti/summary-of-recommendations.html).

**YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.
</details>

### Q70. A urine culture is ordered for a patient with an existing indwelling catheter. Where should a fresh specimen usually be obtained?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** From fluid used to wash the patient's skin
- **B.** By disconnecting the tubing at any point
- **C.** From urine that has been in the drainage bag all day
- **D.** From the designated sampling port using aseptic technique

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. From the designated sampling port using aseptic technique**

Urine culture lab mein microorganisms ki growth check karta hai. Purana bag urine patient ke fresh bladder urine ko accurately represent nahi kar sakta. Fresh sample ke liye designated needleless sampling port ko disinfect karke sterile syringe ya compatible adaptor se aseptic collection karo. Arbitrary tubing puncture mat karo.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Galat):** Skin wash fluid mein urine sample nahi hota aur contamination misleading result de sakti hai.
- **B (Galat):** Tubing disconnect karna unnecessary contamination aur CAUTI risk badhata hai.
- **C (Galat):** Din bhar bag mein pada urine contaminated ya colonized ho sakta hai, isliye culture ke liye appropriate nahi hai.
- **D (Sahi):** Designated port fresh sample lene deta hai aur closed connection preserve karta hai. Sample ko label karke lab instructions follow karo.

**Exam clue:** Culture = fresh aseptic sampling port. Old bag urine ya arbitrary puncture nahi.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://www.cdc.gov/infection-control/hcp/cauti/summary-of-recommendations.html).

**Related exam evidence:** [AIIMS NORCET, 20 November 2021 Shift II — memory-based report](https://testbook.com/question-answer/a-patient-is-unconscious-nurse-is-going-to-take-th--65f82ec5c3d23f0c2a353e20). Reported option 4 uses older ambiguous aspiration wording. Current CDC guidance favors the designated needleless sampling port, not arbitrary tubing puncture.

**YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.
</details>

Source topic Q6.

### Q98. A patient has an indwelling catheter solely because of a now-resolved short-term indication. What is the best next step?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Replace it with a larger catheter regardless of need
- **B.** Clamp it indefinitely to test bladder strength
- **C.** Keep the catheter for the rest of admission automatically
- **D.** Review removal eligibility and remove promptly according to authorized protocol

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Review removal eligibility and remove promptly according to authorized protocol**

Catheter jitne din bladder mein rehti hai, bacteria ko device par settle hone aur infection develop karne ka zyada mauka milta hai. Jab initial indication resolve ho jaaye, removal eligibility check karke authorized nurse-led protocol ya order ke under prompt removal karo. Baad mein voiding aur retention ke signs monitor karo.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Galat):** Larger size lagana resolved indication ko solve nahi karta aur trauma badha sakta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Indefinite clamping bladder distension kar sakti hai. Routine clamping before removal required nahi hai.
- **C (Galat):** Rest of admission tak automatically rakhne se unnecessary catheter-days badhte hain.
- **D (Sahi):** Indication resolve hone par safe removal assess karna infection prevention ka important step hai.

**Exam clue:** Daily review and prompt removal. Routine clamping nahi.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://www.cdc.gov/infection-control/hcp/cauti/summary-of-recommendations.html).

**YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.
</details>

Source topic Q8.

### Q107. Which approach is appropriate for routine meatal hygiene in a catheterized patient?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Avoid all perineal cleaning
- **B.** Use abrasive brushes on the urethral opening
- **C.** Provide routine hygiene and clean after soiling according to policy
- **D.** Apply strong antiseptic repeatedly as a universal CAUTI prevention method

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Provide routine hygiene and clean after soiling according to policy**

Meatus urethra ka external opening hai. Catheter ke around routine gentle cleaning se stool, sweat aur secretions remove hote hain. CAUTI rokne ke liye catheter in place hone par baar-baar antiseptic lagana recommended routine substitute nahi hai. Insertion ke waqt aseptic preparation ek alag baat hai.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Galat):** Cleaning avoid karne se stool aur secretions jama ho sakte hain aur discomfort badhta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Abrasive brush delicate mucosa ko injure kar sakta hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Gentle routine hygiene aur soiling ke baad cleaning skin ko clean aur comfortable rakhte hain.
- **D (Galat):** Strong antiseptics routine preventive benefit establish nahi karte aur tissue irritation kar sakte hain.

**Exam clue:** Routine hygiene during catheter care, sterile technique during acute-care insertion.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://www.cdc.gov/infection-control/hcp/cauti/summary-of-recommendations.html).

**YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.
</details>

### Q16. A patient voids 100 mL and has a large postvoid residual on repeated bladder assessment. Which problem is suggested?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Excessive renal filtration proven by residual volume
- **B.** Normal complete emptying established by the voided volume alone
- **C.** Incomplete bladder emptying
- **D.** Anuria proven by the result

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Incomplete bladder emptying**

Patient ne 100 mL urine pass kiya, lekin baar-baar scan par large PVR mil raha hai. Iska matlab hai ki urine nikalne ke baad bhi bladder poori tarah empty nahi ho raha. Obstruction, bladder muscle weakness ya medicines jaise causes assess kiye ja sakte hain. Ek universal PVR cutoff har patient par apply mat karo.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Galat):** Residual volume bladder emptying ka measure hai, glomerular filtration ka direct measure nahi hai.
- **B (Galat):** Sirf 100 mL voided volume se complete emptying establish nahi hoti, kyunki residual bhi important hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Repeated large residual incomplete bladder emptying suggest karta hai aur further assessment chahiye.
- **D (Galat):** Anuria mein urine production bahut kam ya absent hoti hai. Patient ne urine pass kiya aur bladder mein urine bacha hai, isliye is finding se anuria prove nahi hoti.

**Exam clue:** Voided volume plus PVR tells how well the bladder empties.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK596722/).

**YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.
</details>

Source topic Q10.

### Q32. A timed 24-hour urine collection begins at 7 AM. What is the usual collection procedure?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Collect only nighttime urine
- **B.** Collect the first void and stop before the final scheduled void
- **C.** Discard any specimen with a large volume
- **D.** Discard the initial 7 AM void, then collect all urine including the final 7 AM void next day

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Discard the initial 7 AM void, then collect all urine including the final 7 AM void next day**

Timed collection ka purpose ek fixed 24-hour interval mein excreted substance measure karna hai. Day 1 par 7 AM ka urine discard karke bladder empty karte hain, taaki collection exactly us waqt se start ho. Iske baad har void collect hota hai aur day 2 par 7 AM ka final void bhi include hota hai. Storage, preservative aur missed sample ke liye laboratory instructions follow karo.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Galat):** Sirf raat ka urine collect karna poore din ki excretion nahi batata.
- **B (Galat):** Initial urine mein start se pehle ka urine bhi hota hai aur last void omit karne se measured interval galat ho jaata hai.
- **C (Galat):** Large volume bhi total ka part hai. Use discard karne se measured excretion falsely low ho sakti hai.
- **D (Sahi):** Start-time void discard aur end-time void include karne se poore 24 ghante ka urine milta hai.

**Exam clue:** Start empty, collect all, finish empty at exact end time.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://openstax.org/books/clinical-nursing-skills/pages/10-1-urine-specimen).

**YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.
</details>

Source topic Q12.

### Q99. Which device can noninvasively estimate urine remaining in the bladder after voiding?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Bladder ultrasound scanner
- **B.** Pulse oximeter
- **C.** Peak flow meter
- **D.** Glucometer

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Bladder ultrasound scanner**

Postvoid residual ya PVR urine pass karne ke baad bladder mein bachi quantity hai. Bladder scanner ultrasound waves se volume ka estimate deta hai aur invasive catheterization ke bina retention screen karne mein help karta hai. Result ko symptoms aur clinical context ke saath interpret karo.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Sahi):** Bladder ultrasound scanner urine ke bache volume ka noninvasive estimate deta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Pulse oximeter blood oxygen saturation estimate karta hai, bladder volume nahi.
- **C (Galat):** Peak flow meter saans bahar nikaalne ki maximum flow rate measure karta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Glucometer blood glucose measure karta hai.

**Exam clue:** PVR = bladder volume after voiding, not urine production.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK596722/).

**YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.
</details>

Source topic Q9.

### Q113. Which instruction is appropriate for a midstream clean-catch urine specimen?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Collect urine from the toilet bowl
- **B.** Collect only the first drops in an unclean cup
- **C.** Touch the container interior to stabilize it
- **D.** Begin voiding, then collect the middle portion without touching the inside of the container

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Begin voiding, then collect the middle portion without touching the inside of the container**

Clean-catch sample ka goal urine mein surrounding skin ke germs milne ka risk kam karna hai. Patient ko facility instructions ke mutabik genital hygiene samjhao, first portion toilet mein jaane do aur middle portion sterile container mein collect karvao. Container ke andar ya lid ke inner surface ko touch nahi karna chahiye.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Galat):** Toilet bowl ka water aur microorganisms sample contaminate kar sakte hain.
- **B (Galat):** First drops mein urethral surface ke contaminants aa sakte hain aur unclean cup result ko unreliable banata hai.
- **C (Galat):** Container ka andar touch karne se skin organisms specimen mein aa sakte hain.
- **D (Sahi):** Midstream collection aur container interior untouched rakhne se contamination kam hoti hai.

**Exam clue:** Midstream clean-catch = middle stream, sterile cup, no interior touch.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://openstax.org/books/clinical-nursing-skills/pages/10-1-urine-specimen).

**YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.
</details>

### Q13. What does intermittent catheterization mean?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** The patient never empties the bladder
- **B.** A catheter is inserted into the ureter through the skin in every case
- **C.** A catheter is inserted to drain the bladder and then removed at scheduled or indicated times
- **D.** A catheter remains continuously in the bladder for weeks

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. A catheter is inserted to drain the bladder and then removed at scheduled or indicated times**

Intermittent catheterization mein catheter ko required interval par bladder drain karne ke liye insert kiya jaata hai aur drainage ke baad nikaal diya jaata hai. Isse continuously indwelling device ki zarurat kuch patients mein kam ho sakti hai. Frequency, technique aur training patient aur setting par depend karte hain.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Galat):** Is technique ka purpose bladder empty karna hai, emptying rokna nahi.
- **B (Galat):** Skin se ureter ya kidney tak drainage access ek alag procedure hai, routine intermittent bladder catheterization nahi.
- **C (Sahi):** Required interval par insertion, drainage aur removal is method ki defining feature hai.
- **D (Galat):** Weeks tak continuously rehne wali catheter indwelling catheter hoti hai.

**Exam clue:** Intermittent = insert, drain, remove. Indwelling = stays in place.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK596722/).

**YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.
</details>

Source topic Q15.

### Q20. During catheter insertion a patient experiences severe pain and marked resistance. Which action is safest?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Stop advancing and seek appropriate clinical assistance
- **B.** Use a larger catheter automatically
- **C.** Inflate the balloon immediately despite uncertain placement
- **D.** Push the catheter forcefully past resistance

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Stop advancing and seek appropriate clinical assistance**

Marked resistance aur severe pain catheter ka wrong path, obstruction ya urethral injury ka warning sign ho sakte hain. Force lagane se false passage, bleeding aur further trauma ho sakta hai. Nurse advancement stop karke patient assess karti hai aur appropriate experienced clinician ki help leti hai.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Sahi):** Stop aur seek assistance se further trauma avoid hota hai aur cause safely evaluate ho sakta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Bina assessment larger catheter try karne se obstruction aur tissue injury worse ho sakte hain.
- **C (Galat):** Uncertain placement mein balloon inflate karne se urethra stretch ya tear ho sakti hai.
- **D (Galat):** Forceful advancement urethral wall ko damage kar sakti hai.

**Exam clue:** Resistance or severe pain means stop, never force.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK596722/).

**YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.
</details>

Source topic Q16.

### Q68. A catheterized patient develops fever and new flank pain. What is the appropriate nursing response?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Diagnose infection solely from cloudy urine
- **B.** Ignore symptoms because a catheter is present
- **C.** Automatically start an unprescribed antibiotic
- **D.** Assess for infection and other causes, escalate and collect specimens only as indicated

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Assess for infection and other causes, escalate and collect specimens only as indicated**

Flank pain side ya back mein kidney ke area ka dard hai. Catheterized patient mein fever aur new flank pain upper urinary tract infection ya kisi aur serious problem ka signal ho sakta hai. Nurse vital signs, pain, urine output aur overall condition assess karti hai, sepsis ke signs par urgent escalation karti hai aur indicated specimens protocol ke hisaab se collect karti hai.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Galat):** Cloudy urine alone se symptomatic infection diagnose nahi hoti. Colonization ya sediment bhi ho sakta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Catheter infection risk ko eliminate nahi karti. New fever aur pain ignore karna unsafe hai.
- **C (Galat):** Unprescribed antibiotics dena unsafe hai aur culture interpretation aur antimicrobial resistance par asar daal sakta hai. Urgent prescribed treatment ko delay bhi nahi karna chahiye.
- **D (Sahi):** Assessment, timely escalation aur clinically indicated culture appropriate response hai.

**Exam clue:** Symptoms and systemic assessment matter more than urine appearance alone.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://www.cdc.gov/uti/hcp/clinical-guidance/index.html).

**YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.
</details>

Source topic Q14.

### Q69. A urinary drainage bag needs emptying. Which technique reduces cross-contamination?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Use the same unclean jug for every patient
- **B.** Place the outlet on the floor while measuring
- **C.** Use a separate clean collection container and avoid outlet contact with the container
- **D.** Touch the drainage outlet to the shared measuring jug

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Use a separate clean collection container and avoid outlet contact with the container**

Bag empty karte waqt outlet aur collection container ke beech direct contact se microorganisms transfer ho sakte hain. Har patient ke liye separate clean measuring container use karo, splash avoid karo, outlet ko container se touch na hone do aur hand hygiene follow karo. Measured output accurately document karo.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Galat):** Unclean shared jug microorganisms carry kar sakta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Floor contaminated surface ho sakta hai. Outlet ko floor par rakhne se drainage system contaminate ho sakta hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Separate container aur no-touch drainage se cross-contamination kam hoti hai.
- **D (Galat):** Shared jug ko outlet touch karne se germs ek patient se doosre ke equipment tak ja sakte hain.

**Exam clue:** Dedicated clean jug, no outlet contact, measure and record.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://www.cdc.gov/infection-control/hcp/cauti/summary-of-recommendations.html).

**YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.
</details>

### Q46. Before inflating an indwelling urinary catheter balloon, what must be confirmed?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Correct bladder placement according to the insertion protocol
- **B.** That the balloon is positioned in the urethra
- **C.** That the drainage bag has already been disconnected
- **D.** That the patient feels severe urethral pain

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Correct bladder placement according to the insertion protocol**

Foley balloon ek chhota retaining balloon hai jo bladder ke andar inflated rehkar catheter ko place par rakhta hai. Urethra mein balloon inflate karne se serious trauma ho sakta hai. Urine return aur protocol ke mutabik sufficient advancement se bladder placement confirm karo. Agar placement uncertain ho toh balloon inflate na karo aur assistance lo.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Sahi):** Correct bladder placement confirm karna balloon inflation ki necessary safety condition hai.
- **B (Galat):** Urethra mein balloon inflate karna tissue injury aur bleeding cause kar sakta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Bag disconnect karna bladder placement prove nahi karta aur infection risk badhata hai.
- **D (Galat):** Severe pain warning sign hai, correct placement ka proof nahi.

**Exam clue:** Urine return alone may not establish balloon position. Follow device-specific insertion protocol.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK596722/).

**YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.
</details>

Source topic Q17.

### Q51. A postoperative patient has low urine output despite a patent catheter. Which assessment is most appropriate?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Give a large unprescribed fluid bolus to every patient
- **B.** Document normal output without measuring
- **C.** Assume catheter replacement alone will restore urine production
- **D.** Assess fluid balance, perfusion, vital signs and possible renal causes and escalate as indicated

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Assess fluid balance, perfusion, vital signs and possible renal causes and escalate as indicated**

Patent catheter ka matlab hai drainage pathway open hai. Phir bhi low urine output ho toh low circulating volume, bleeding, poor perfusion, acute kidney injury ya postoperative factors assess karo. Vitals, intake-output trend, fluid status aur relevant labs review karo. At-risk adults mein 0.5 mL/kg/hour se kam output ek important warning threshold hai, lekin urgent clinical response ke liye diagnostic duration ka wait mat karo.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Galat):** Har patient ko large unprescribed bolus dene se heart ya kidney problem mein overload ho sakta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Measurement ke bina normal output document karna inaccurate aur unsafe hai.
- **C (Galat):** Patent catheter replace karna kidney perfusion ya urine production problem ka direct treatment nahi hai.
- **D (Sahi):** Whole-patient assessment low urine production ki possible cause identify karta hai aur timely treatment guide karta hai.

**Exam clue:** Patent catheter plus oliguria = assess perfusion and renal causes, not automatic fluids.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng148/chapter/Recommendations).

**YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.
</details>

Source topic Q20.

### Q67. Which intervention supports dignity for a patient who needs help using a bedpan?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Provide privacy, explain the procedure and ensure timely assistance
- **B.** Leave the door open without consent
- **C.** Delay assistance until the patient becomes incontinent
- **D.** Discuss the patient's elimination loudly in the corridor

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Provide privacy, explain the procedure and ensure timely assistance**

Bedpan ki zarurat patient ki personal elimination need hai. Nurse privacy provide karti hai, procedure explain karti hai aur patient ko safe position mein timely help deti hai. Call bell accessible rakho aur skin hygiene aur comfort ka dhyan rakho. Patient ki dignity care ka essential part hai.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Sahi):** Privacy, explanation aur timely assistance patient ki comfort, autonomy aur trust protect karte hain.
- **B (Galat):** Bina consent door khula rakhne se personal privacy compromise ho sakti hai.
- **C (Galat):** Help delay karne se discomfort, incontinence, skin exposure aur unsafe independent movement ho sakte hain.
- **D (Galat):** Corridor mein personal information loudly discuss karna confidentiality breach hai.

**Exam clue:** Privacy and timely assistance are core nursing care.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://openstax.org/books/clinical-nursing-skills/pages/19-4-nursing-management-of-elimination).

**YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.
</details>

Source topic Q18.

### Q77. A patient with functional incontinence can sense bladder fullness but cannot reach the toilet in time due to limited mobility. Which plan addresses the main problem?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Provide accessible toileting, scheduled assistance and suitable mobility support
- **B.** Restrict all fluid intake throughout the day
- **C.** Insert an indwelling catheter routinely without reviewing alternatives
- **D.** Assume permanent loss of bladder sensation

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Provide accessible toileting, scheduled assistance and suitable mobility support**

Functional incontinence mein patient ko bladder fullness ka pata ho sakta hai, lekin mobility, cognition ya environment ki wajah se toilet tak time par nahi pahunch pata. Is case mein limited mobility main barrier hai. Accessible commode, scheduled assistance, call bell aur safe mobility support se main problem address hoti hai.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Sahi):** Accessible toilet aur scheduled safe help patient ko time par bladder empty karne mein support karte hain.
- **B (Galat):** Complete fluid restriction se dehydration ho sakti hai. Fluids individualized clinical plan ke mutabik dene chahiye.
- **C (Galat):** Routine indwelling catheter se infection aur injury risk badhta hai aur mobility barrier solve nahi hota.
- **D (Galat):** Stem mein bladder sensation present hai. Permanent sensation loss assume karna evidence ke against hai.

**Exam clue:** Functional incontinence = access barrier. Improve access rather than routine catheter.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://openstax.org/books/clinical-nursing-skills/pages/19-4-nursing-management-of-elimination).

**YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.
</details>

### PYQ6. During female urinary catheter preparation, which cleaning direction helps avoid transfer of organisms from the anal area toward the urethra?

**Reported exam:** NORCET 4, 2023, reported paper transcription

[Question source](https://nextnurse.in/pyq/norcet/norcet-norcet-4)

- **A.** Front to back with the approved aseptic technique
- **B.** Back to front with one reused swab
- **C.** Repeated wiping from the anus toward the urethra
- **D.** No cleaning before insertion

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Front to back with the approved aseptic technique**

Female urinary meatus anus ke paas hota hai. Anus ke area mein gut bacteria ho sakte hain, isliye cleansing front se back ki taraf ki jaati hai. Acute-care catheter insertion mein approved aseptic preparation aur fresh sterile supplies follow karna zaroori hai. Routine catheter maintenance hygiene ko insertion preparation se confuse mat karo.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Sahi):** Front-to-back cleaning anus se urethra ki taraf contamination transfer ka risk kam karti hai. Approved insertion protocol follow karna chahiye.
- **B (Galat):** Back-to-front wiping anal organisms urethral opening tak la sakti hai. Used swab reuse karna contamination aur badha sakta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Anus se urethra ki taraf repeatedly wiping karne se contamination ka risk badhta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Insertion se pehle indicated aseptic preparation skip karna infection prevention ke against hai.

**Exam clue:** Front to back during preparation, each swab as protocol directs.

**Clinical reference:** [CDC CAUTI recommendations](https://www.cdc.gov/infection-control/hcp/cauti/summary-of-recommendations.html). Historical source attribution pending direct verification. **YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific verification pending.

</details>

### PYQ1. Which general nursing measure prevents traction on an indwelling urinary catheter?

**Reported exam:** PGIMER Nursing Officer, 2020

[Question source](https://nprep.in/question-answer/a-patient-with-urinary-catheterization-is-admitted-to-the-ward-what-should-jlsUytxqVRurBzpBd2WXD)

- **A.** Secure the catheter using an appropriate device with slack
- **B.** Leave the drainage bag hanging from the catheter
- **C.** Tie tubing tightly to a moving side rail
- **D.** Remove every securement device during movement

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Secure the catheter using an appropriate device with slack**

Urinary catheter par tension se urethral lining injure ho sakti hai. Securement device catheter ko stable rakhta hai, slack patient ki movement allow karta hai aur drainage bag ka weight separately support hota hai. Securement location patient ki anatomy, device aur facility policy ke hisaab se choose karo.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Sahi):** Suitable device aur slack urethral traction kam karte hain.
- **B (Galat):** Heavy bag catheter se latkane par bag ka weight urethra par pull karta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Moving rail catheter ko kheench sakti hai, especially jab rail reposition hoti hai.
- **D (Galat):** Securement remove karne se patient movement catheter par transfer ho sakti hai.

**Exam clue:** Secure catheter and bag separately, no traction.

**Clinical reference:** [CDC CAUTI recommendations](https://www.cdc.gov/infection-control/hcp/cauti/summary-of-recommendations.html). Historical source attribution pending direct verification. **YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific verification pending.

</details>

### PYQ2. For a female patient with a urinary catheter, where is a suitable securement device commonly placed if consistent with local policy?

**Reported exam:** PGIMER Sangrur Nursing Officer, 2023

[Question source](https://nprep.in/question-answer/a-female-patient-with-urinary-catheterization-is-admitted-to-the-ward-what-yHWA4fJ21qaSGO5pHApTH)

- **A.** Directly around the urethral opening under tension
- **B.** On a moving side rail
- **C.** On the opposite bed without slack
- **D.** Upper thigh with slack to avoid traction

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Upper thigh with slack to avoid traction**

Female catheter ki tubing ko commonly upper thigh par appropriate device se secure kiya ja sakta hai. Isse patient movement ke waqt urethral opening par tension kam hoti hai. Correct site device instructions aur local policy par depend karti hai, isliye upper thigh ko har situation ka universal rule mat samjho.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Galat):** Urethral opening par direct tension mucosa ko injure kar sakti hai.
- **B (Galat):** Moving rail ka position change catheter kheench sakta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Opposite bed par bina slack fixation patient movement restrict karti hai aur traction badhati hai.
- **D (Sahi):** Upper thigh par suitable securement aur slack commonly appropriate hai, agar protocol permit kare.

**Exam clue:** Site is individualized, the principle is zero urethral traction.

**Clinical reference:** [CDC CAUTI recommendations](https://www.cdc.gov/infection-control/hcp/cauti/summary-of-recommendations.html). Historical source attribution pending direct verification. **YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific verification pending.

</details>

### PYQ3. Which routine practice is inappropriate for catheter-associated urinary tract infection prevention?

**Reported exam:** SGPGI Nursing Officer, 2022

[Question source](https://nprep.in/question-answer/which-of-the-following-interventions-is-not-included-in-the-prevention-of-DYbU_Vku_z8etLmvNrUo2)

- **A.** Remove the catheter when no longer indicated
- **B.** Perform hand hygiene before and after handling the system
- **C.** Disconnect the closed drainage system repeatedly without clinical need
- **D.** Maintain unobstructed urine flow

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Disconnect the closed drainage system repeatedly without clinical need**

CAUTI catheter-associated urinary tract infection hai. Unnecessary catheter use aur open drainage connections bacteria ko urinary tract tak pahunchne ka chance dete hain. Closed drainage, hand hygiene, unobstructed flow aur prompt removal main prevention measures hain. Agar system compromise ho toh authorized aseptic replacement protocol follow karo.

**Har option ka reason**

- **A (Galat):** Indication khatam hone par removal catheter exposure kam karti hai. Yeh recommended measure hai.
- **B (Galat):** Handling se pehle aur baad hand hygiene microorganisms transfer ka risk kam karti hai. Yeh appropriate measure hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Repeated unnecessary disconnection contamination ka rasta kholti hai. Yeh inappropriate practice hai aur negative stem ka correct answer hai.
- **D (Galat):** Unobstructed flow maintain karna urine stagnation aur backflow risk kam karne mein madad karta hai. Yeh appropriate measure hai.

**Exam clue:** Negative stem: identify the unsafe action, not the prevention measure.

**Clinical reference:** [CDC CAUTI recommendations](https://www.cdc.gov/infection-control/hcp/cauti/summary-of-recommendations.html). Historical source attribution pending direct verification. **YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific verification pending.

</details>
